findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REEPAT x2) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sanitizers in the facility did not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was consulted and stated that they had changed to a different chemical (Purrell) and mixed it with water as they used to do with bleach. Education was conducted. The Purrell chemical is not a concentrate and should be used as-is out of the bottle for effective sanitizing of food contact surfaces. They were instructed to remake their buckets/bottles to be at effective concentrations. A bucket was made using CL/bleach instead. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times that food handling is taking place in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

On arrival multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine were observed soiled and in need of cleaning. The PIC was shown and cleaned the nozzles during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized regularly to prevent the accumulation of filth and likely contamination of foods in the  facility.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Numerous flies were observed throughout the kitchen and service areas of the facility, particularly around the fountain drink machine. The PIC was shown and discussed. They stated that they tried vinegar and then contacted their pest control for remediation. The inspector will give three weeks for the remedial action to take place prior to following up.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The facility was using an alcohol based sanitizer (Purrell) and only had test strips effective for testing CL based sanitizers. Education was conducted and the PIC changed the in use sanitizer to a CL based chemical (bleach). This corrects the immediate violation. Ensure that the available sanitizers and test strips match moving forward.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. The situation was discussed and someone who said that they had a CFPM arrived during this inspection, however a certification was not available for this person at the facility. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs working at the facility to ensure that all shifts are covered when food handling is taking place.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

There is not currently a verification method available at the facility for employees acknowledging their responsibility to report food safety symptoms and diagnosis. A fresh copy of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreement was given to the PIC. They are instructed to make copies and have all employees sign a copy prior to the follow up in 10 day.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

A food handler was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with all employees and enforce safe food handling practices at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink in the facility is without soap. Soap was provided to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks in the facility are supplied with soap at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT X2) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Large accumulations of mold are observed on the baffle in the ice machine. Education conducted and this items will be checked at the follow-up being conducted in 10 days. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained cleaned and sanitized at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REEPAT) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). 

On arrival the spray bottle labeled for sanitizer did not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was consulted and was instructed to remake the solution. A bucket was made using CL/bleach instead. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times that food handling is taking place in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

An employee was observed to use a dry wiping cloth on the cutting board and knife used for sandwich preparation during this inspection. This should have been a sani rag stored in solution between uses to prevent the growth of pathogenic organisms. Education was conducted and the rag moved to the newly created sani bucket to correct.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

Degreaser and window cleaner are observed in spray bottles without labels. The PIC was shown and instructed to add labels to the containers. Labels were added to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips were not available for the sanitizer used in the facility. The PIC was consulted and instructed to acquire test strips effective for the sanitizers used in the facility prior to the follow-up in 10 days.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Food handler cards are not available for the staff at this facility at the time of this inspection. The situation was discussed and the PIC instructed to ensure that food handler cards are maintained at the facility for all food handlers in the facility at all times.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Facility only has 1 CFM and they are not present at time of inspection. Discussed with PIC. A certified food manager must be present at all hours of operation, all other staff must have a food handler’s card. Will follow up at next routine inspection. See that adequate CFMs are on staff to cover hours of operation.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Staff did not demonstrate knowledge of the food operation in the following areas: Use of sanitizers during food preparation (see #16 and #28). Staff was not aware of proper holding temperatures for TCS foods when asked by inspector (see #22). Follow up to occur to ensure staff have been properly trained on handwashing, sanitation, cold holding.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Neither worker present at time of inspection is a CFPM. Ensure a CFPM is present during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment: Staff does not have employee health reporting agreements on file. Will address at 3-day follow up.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Procedure for vomit/diarrhea cleanup not available. Will go over at follow up.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. 

Employee personal drinks stored in deli cooler, where customer food is held. Discussed with PIC. Store employee drinks away from customer food prep and storage areas at all times.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. P (C) PACKAGED Food shall be properly labeled.

Packages of turkey bacon in cooler not labeled with any manufacturer information. Photos taken of suspect food. Discussed with PIC. Food must be labeled properly for retail sale and must be from an approved source. See #22. Food voluntarily discarded.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

Upon inspector arrival staff member observed preparing sandwiches on cutting board. On cutting board, staff member had propped a cell phone and was viewing a movie. Discussed with PIC. Do not place personal items in direct contact with food preparation surfaces. Cell phones should only be used in designated areas away from food prep areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
34-501.114  (P) No sanitizer is in use at facility to properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces in between sandwich orders. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration sanitizer bucket during all hours of operation. Reference 4-501.114.

No sanitation available At time of inspection. Inspector observed staff making sandwiches. Inspector asked what sanitizer they used, they pointed to a bottle of degreaser. When inspector advised that is not a sanitizer, they then pointed to isopropyl alcohol. Discussed acceptable sanitizers in food service. Advised staff to purchase proper bleach (see #28).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Food in glass coolers observed to be out of acceptable temperature ranges per food code. Staff aware walk-in cooler was not functioning properly and unsure of how long food had been out of temperature. Photos taken of probed items. The following items voluntarily discarded: 19 1/2 gal milk probed at 48, 9 1 gal milk probed at 50, 9 1-doz carton of eggs probed at 50, 29 lunchables, 14 hot dog packages probed 48, 6 bacon probed at 50, 15 shredded cheese probed at 53. Follow up issued, pending repairs and phone call from facility for re-inspection.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

Bottle of purple cleaner not labeled. PIC identified it as degreaser. Ensure bottles of chemicals are properly labeled. COS- PIC labeled bottle.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

Bleach is not approved as a sanitizer in food service. Purchase bleach that meets the following criteria: has EPA registration label, has directions to make ppm concentration, specifies use on food contact surfaces/dishes/kitchen, etc.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Neither staff member present possesses a valid food handler card. Ensure all staff present who prepare food have a valid food handlers card and keep on hand to present to inspectors.

Observed food employee changing gloves without washing hands in between making sandwiches for multiple customers. Ensure hands are washed in between glove changes and in between tasks.

Facility is moving a bottle of dishsoap in between handwashing station and the 3 compartment sink. Ensure handsoap is kept at handwashing sink at all times. Do not use dish soap as a replacement of handsoap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-501.114  (P) No sanitizer bucket is in use at facility to properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces in between sandwich orders. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration sanitizer bucket during all hours of operation. Reference 4-501.114.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
Observed heavy mold buildup dripping into ice in ice machine out back. Ensure all existing ice is discarded and the entire interior of the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items in deli display case. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was relabeled. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple sliced lunch meats without a date mark, along with sliced vegetables. PIC stated they were prepared the evening before. Inspector explained applicable sections of the food code and food was labeled appropriately.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.
Observed employee wiping down cutting board in between sandwich orders with a soiled rag. Ensure rags are kept in a properly concentrated sanitizer bucket to prevent bacterial growth.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a container of tomatoes and all deli meats in the sliding cooler with no date mark. Provide a date mark on all potentially hazardous foods. A date mark was provided on all tomatoes and deli meats during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated

750-160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.

750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.
